evals.name: python-api-overview
evals.prompt: I just inherited this Python service and I have no clue how it works. It's at /Users/maoryosef/.claude/skills/codebase-flow-maps-workspace/test-repos/pyshop. Can you map out the main flows so I can get oriented before I start making changes?
evals.expected_output: A committed Markdown doc with several Mermaid diagrams: a module/dependency map plus the order request lifecycle and data flow. Diagrams trace real code (app.py route -> auth -> order_service.create_order -> inventory -> payment -> db) with file:line citations. Valid Mermaid, readable altitude, honest about anything untraced.
expectations: Output includes a Markdown file with at least two distinct ```mermaid diagrams
One diagram is a module/dependency map of the pyshop components (app, auth, services, db)
The order-creation flow is shown end-to-end: HTTP entry -> auth check -> order_service.create_order -> inventory reserve -> payment charge -> db save
The doc cites specific file:line locations, and every cited file path exists in the pyshop repo
All Mermaid diagrams are structurally valid (recognized diagram header, matched subgraph/end pairs)
The failure branches (out of stock / payment declined) or the Order status transitions (pending->reserved->paid/failed) are represented

evals.name: ts-state-machine-targeted
evals.prompt: Diagram the job lifecycle in this worker at /Users/maoryosef/.claude/skills/codebase-flow-maps-workspace/test-repos/jobworker. I specifically want to see the state machine — how a job moves from queued through running to success or failure, including the retry path and when it gives up.
evals.expected_output: A state diagram (Mermaid stateDiagram-v2) showing queued -> running -> succeeded/failed, the failed -> queued retry edge, and failed/exhausted -> dead. Transitions labeled with the triggering functions (markRunning/markSucceeded/markFailed) traced to src/job.ts. Focused on the requested target rather than the whole repo.
expectations: The diagram contains the states a job actually enters: queued, running, succeeded, and dead
Both the retry path (running -> queued on failure while attempts remain) and the give-up path (running -> dead when attempts are exhausted) are shown
Transitions are labeled with / attributed to the triggering functions (markRunning/markSucceeded/markFailed) and traced to src/job.ts
Every cited file path exists in the jobworker repo
GROUNDING: correctly handles that the 'failed' state in the JobState union is never assigned (flags it as dead code or omits it) rather than drawing a fictitious failed-> transition

evals.name: go-architecture-shareable
evals.prompt: Give me a visual architecture overview of this Go repo at /Users/maoryosef/.claude/skills/codebase-flow-maps-workspace/test-repos/goshort that I can share with my team to explain how the URL shortener works.
evals.expected_output: An architecture/module map plus the request lifecycle (main -> handler -> shortener + cache -> store) and the cache-in-front-of-store data flow. Diagrams grounded in real code with file:line citations. Given 'share with my team', either a clean Markdown doc or an HTML artifact is acceptable.
expectations: Output includes a module/architecture map showing main -> handler -> (shortener, cache) -> store
The request lifecycle for at least one route (/shorten or /r/{code}) is diagrammed from HTTP entry to the store
The cache-in-front-of-store behavior (read-through / write-through) is represented
The doc cites specific file:line locations, and every cited file path exists in the goshort repo
All diagrams are structurally valid Mermaid; if an HTML page is produced it is self-contained (no external network dependencies)
Every component shown corresponds to a real package/file in the repo (no invented components)
